summary.text: Furrion FFG20, FFG30 and FFG35 RV furnaces are 12V DC propane furnaces with automatic ignition and a wall thermostat. They have no owner-readable fault display: a fault puts the furnace into lockout, and the lockout error code can only be retrieved by a qualified RV service provider using a Furrion Furnace diagnostic PCB.

models.text: The troubleshooting manual covers FFG20FA, FFG20RA, FFG30FA, FFG30RA, FFG35FA and FFG35RA, plus the second-generation FFG20FA2, FFG20RA2, FFG30FA2, FFG30RA2, FFG35FA2 and FFG35RA2.
FA models use the Front Gas Tube Kit and RA models use the Rear Gas Tube, i.e. front versus rear gas connection.
BTU/hr input and 12V DC power input are printed on the appliance rating tag; the approved gas type is on the furnace rating plate.
Owner instruction manuals: CCD-0006025 for the FA/RA furnaces and CCD-0009365 (V2) for FFG20FA2/RA2, FFG30FA2/RA2 and FFG35FA2/RA2.

display.text: There is no fault display for owners. In lockout the furnace produces an error code that only a qualified RV service provider can retrieve with a Furrion Furnace diagnostic PCB.
The furnace has an automatic ignition device and no pilot. After the thermostat calls for heat, allow thirty (30) seconds for the main burner to light; if it does not, the furnace may be in lockout.
During initial firing, burn-off of leftover paint and oils from manufacturing may cause 'smoking' for 5-10 minutes.

reset.text: Lockout causes listed: air in the propane line after long non-use, empty or low propane (a cold tank may not keep flow), blocked exhaust or intake, blocked supply/return vents or crushed ductwork, and a sticky sail switch.

Thermostat Reset: wait until the blower stops; thermostat OFF and wait 60 seconds; ON in heat above room temperature; within 10 seconds OFF; within 10 seconds ON again. The furnace then attempts ignition.
Thermostats have different built-in switching delays; listening for a click at the thermostat or controller helps with the reset timing.
Power Reset: wait until the blower stops, then remove power from the furnace for approximately 5 minutes, for example by removing and reinstalling the fuse.
If air is in the propane line, repeat the reset up to 3 times, waiting 5 minutes between attempts.

checks.text: For 'Furnace will not light – Blower does not turn on' the table starts with: reset power to the furnace, confirm gas valves are ON and tanks not empty, and check the main fuse panel for a blown fuse.
Next in the same table: check RV system voltage because low 12V DC power stops the furnace, then clear a possible lockout using the lockout steps.
Then check that the intake and vents are not blocked or obstructed.
Air in the LP line: purge it by turning on other gas appliances, such as a cooktop, that are further downstream from the LP tanks.
Last, confirm the thermostat is set to Heat and to a high enough temperature.
If the furnace shuts off before reaching the set temperature, make sure all vents are open and uncovered and the air intake is not blocked.
Turn the manual valve or outside LP tank valve fully ON by hand; never operate with the valve partially closed and never use tools on the gas control valve.
Do not restrict ducting or block outlet registers and return-air grilles, and do not install screens over the air intake or exhaust vents.
Inspect the vent monthly during the heating season for soot, and keep the furnace, control compartment and air passageways clean of lint from carpet, bedding and pet hair.

parts.text: Sail switch (Lippert 2023010310): a sticky sail switch is a listed lockout cause; replacement is service work, as the manual says never attempt to repair the furnace yourself.
Control board (Active Low Input), part 2023010309 or 2023060551, listed for all models; service technician part.

Igniter electrode 2023010317, furnace burner 2023010318, gas solenoid valve 2023010319 and HI limit switch 2023010322 are the ignition and safety parts in the parts list; use only Furrion approved replacements installed by a qualified technician.
'Diagnose PCB Units' (2023010324) is the Furrion furnace diagnostic PCB that service providers use to read lockout error codes.
Furnace-installed breaker switch: if it is tripped or OFF, the manual says contact a trained RV service provider.

callTech.text: If you smell gas: evacuate everyone, shut off gas at the container, do not touch electrical switches, phones or radios, do not start the engine or generator, and call the gas supplier, a qualified technician or the fire department.
If the furnace still does not ignite after 3 reset attempts, contact a qualified RV service provider; do not keep cycling the thermostat to light it.
Immediately shut down the furnace and call a service agency if it cycles erratically or delays on ignition.
If the gas supply fails to shut off or overheating occurs, shut off the gas valve to the furnace before shutting off the electrical supply.
Soot on the vent: immediately shut the furnace down and contact a qualified service agency.
A yellow or lazy burner flame instead of a hard blue flame means shut the furnace down; the burner may need cleaning or replacement by a qualified person.
Do not use the furnace if any part has been under water; a qualified service agency must inspect it and replace wet gas controls and electrical parts.
Have a qualified person inspect the furnace yearly before use, including gas leak and pressure-drop tests, burner and orifice inspection, venting and wiring.
